cards.canonical_statement: On any nontrivial finite-dimensional real inner-product space, every negative multiple c‖x‖² has gradient zero at the origin but does not have a local minimum there. Stationarity alone is not a sufficient minimum criterion.
cards.proof_strategy: Differentiate the scaled squared norm to obtain gradient zero at the origin.
sketch_steps: Differentiate the scaled squared norm to obtain gradient zero at the origin.
Choose a nonzero direction u.
Every neighborhood of zero contains a small positive multiple of u.
At that point c‖x‖² is strictly negative, contradicting the local minimum inequality.

cards.lean_witness:
by
 constructor
 · apply hasGradientAt_iff_hasFDerivAt.mpr
   convert! (hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq (0 : E)).hasFDerivAt.const_smul c using 1 <;> ext y <;> simp
 · intro h
   obtain ⟨δ,hδ,hh⟩ := Metric.eventually_nhds_iff.mp h
   have hn : 0 < ‖u‖ := norm_pos_iff.mpr hu
   let t := δ / (2 * ‖u‖)
   have ht : 0 < t := by dsimp [t]; positivity
   have hnorm : ‖t • u‖ = δ / 2 := by rw [norm_smul,Real.norm_eq_abs,abs_of_pos ht]; dsimp [t]; field_simp
   have hd : dist (t • u) 0 < δ := by simpa [dist_zero_right,hnorm] using (show δ / 2 < δ by linarith)
   have hv := hh hd
   simp only [norm_zero,zero_pow (by decide : 2 ≠ 0),mul_zero,hnorm] at hv
   have hp : 0 < (δ / 2)^2 := sq_pos_of_pos (by positivity)
   nlinarith [mul_neg_of_neg_of_pos hc hp]

cards.canonical_statement: On any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with a nonzero vector, there exists a function with a local minimum at the origin that is not differentiable there. A local minimum does not imply the differentiability premise of Fermat’s theorem.
cards.proof_strategy: Use the norm function as the witness.
sketch_steps: Use the norm function as the witness.
Nonnegativity makes the origin a global, hence local, minimum.
The supplied nonzero vector makes the space nontrivial.
The norm on a nontrivial real normed space is not differentiable at zero.

cards.canonical_statement: For c>0 on any finite-dimensional real inner-product space, a point x is a local minimum of c‖·‖² exactly when x=0. This recognizes all local minimizers of the positive definite radial quadratic.
sketch_steps: Differentiate the scaled squared norm.
At a local minimum its derivative must vanish.
Evaluating that derivative on x and using c>0 forces x=0.
Conversely, nonnegativity proves that zero is a global and local minimum.

cards.canonical_statement: For every nonnegative c and every finite-dimensional real inner-product space, the origin is a local and global minimizer of c‖x‖². The conclusion allows c=0 and does not claim uniqueness.
cards.proof_strategy: The squared norm is nonnegative everywhere.
sketch_steps: The squared norm is nonnegative everywhere.
Multiplication by c≥0 preserves that inequality.
The objective has value zero at the origin, so the global minimum inequality follows.
A global minimum is in particular a local minimum.

cards.canonical_statement: For a continuous linear map A between finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces, any exact solution Ax=b globally and locally minimizes the squared residual ‖Ay−b‖² and has zero objective gradient. Neither uniqueness nor existence of an exact solution is asserted without the supplied solution.
cards.proof_strategy: The given exact solution has residual zero.
sketch_steps: The given exact solution has residual zero.
Every squared residual is nonnegative, proving global and local optimality.
Differentiate the affine residual using the linear map A.
Compose with the squared-norm derivative; the zero residual makes the derivative and gradient vanish.

cards.lean_target: example (E F : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℝ F] [FiniteDimensional ℝ F] (A : E →L[ℝ] F) (b : F) (x : E) (hx : A x = b) : IsLocalMin (fun y => ‖A y - b‖^2) x ∧ (∀ y, ‖A x - b‖^2 ≤ ‖A y - b‖^2) ∧ HasGradientAt (fun y => ‖A y - b‖^2) 0 x
cards.lean_witness:
by
 have h : ∀ y, ‖A x - b‖^2 ≤ ‖A y - b‖^2 := by intro y; simpa [hx] using sq_nonneg ‖A y - b‖
 refine ⟨Filter.Eventually.of_forall h,h,?_⟩
 apply hasGradientAt_iff_hasFDerivAt.mpr
 have hd := (hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq (A x - b)).hasFDerivAt.comp x (A.hasFDerivAt.sub_const b)
 convert! hd using 1 <;> ext y <;> simp [hx]
